question: How many of the first \(2018\) numbers in the sequence \(101,\) \(1001,\) \(10001,\) \(100001,\) \(\ldots\) are divisible by \(101?\)
solution:
The first \(2018\) terms are \(10^n+1\) for \(n=2,3,\ldots,2019\). The key observation is
\[
100\equiv-1\pmod{101},
\]
so powers of \(100\) have alternating remainders \(-1\) and \(1\).

If \(n=2k\) is even, then
\[
10^n+1=100^k+1\equiv(-1)^k+1\pmod{101}.
\]
For odd \(k\), this is \(0\); for even \(k\), it is \(2\). Thus the successful even exponents are precisely
\[
n=2,6,10,\ldots,2018.
\]

If \(n=2k+1\) is odd, then
\[
10^n+1=10\cdot100^k+1
\equiv10(-1)^k+1\pmod{101}.
\]
This is either \(11\) or \(-9\), neither of which is divisible by \(101\). Therefore no odd exponent works.

The successful exponents start at \(2\), end at \(2018\), and increase by \(4\), so their number is
\[
\frac{2018-2}{4}+1=504+1=\boxed{505}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{C}\).
